text: The CDC recommends that most adults get a seasonal flu vaccine each year.
headline: The claim is accurate but understates the CDC's recommendation. Per CDC/ACIP policy, annual flu vaccination is recommended for all persons aged 6 months and older without a contraindication — not just 'most adults.'

text: Multiple large studies have found no link between childhood vaccines and autism.
headline: This claim is strongly supported by the scientific consensus. Decades of independent research across multiple countries consistently find no causal link between childhood vaccines and autism. Important context: in November 2025, the CDC's website was revised under HHS Secretary RFK Jr. to cast doubt on this consensus — a move widely condemned by scientists and medical organizations as scientifically inaccurate.

text: The U.S. federal minimum wage has been $7.25 an hour since 2009.
headline: This claim is accurate. The U.S. federal minimum wage has been $7.25 per hour since July 24, 2009 — the longest stretch without an increase in the history of the Fair Labor Standards Act.

text: U.S. federal government spending has exceeded revenue every year for the past two decades, adding to the national debt.
headline: The claim is accurate and well-supported by official records. The U.S. Treasury confirms FY 2001 was the last surplus year ($127 billion), and every fiscal year from FY 2002 through FY 2025 has recorded a deficit — a streak of 23+ consecutive years. The FY 2025 deficit was $1.78 trillion. Each deficit adds to the national debt via government borrowing.

text: U.S. Customs and Border Protection publishes monthly statistics on Southwest border encounters.
headline: This claim is accurate and confirmed by retrieved page content. CBP maintains a dedicated Southwest Land Border Encounters dashboard and issues monthly press releases with encounter figures; the data covers USBP apprehensions, OFO inadmissibles, and Title 42 expulsions.

text: Several peer-reviewed studies have found that immigrants, including undocumented immigrants, are not more likely to commit violent crimes than native-born citizens.
headline: The post's claim is accurate — and is if anything an understatement. Multiple peer-reviewed and government-funded studies consistently find that immigrants, including undocumented immigrants, commit crimes at lower rates than native-born citizens, not merely at equal rates. A minority of dissenting research exists, and real methodological caveats apply.

text: Same-sex marriage has been legal nationwide in the United States since the 2015 Supreme Court ruling in Obergefell v. Hodges.
headline: The claim is accurate. Obergefell v. Hodges, decided June 26, 2015, established a constitutional right to same-sex marriage in all 50 states via a 5–4 ruling authored by Justice Anthony Kennedy. The 2022 Respect for Marriage Act (effective December 13, 2022) later added a statutory backstop at the federal level.

text: A number of U.S. states have passed laws restricting transgender athletes' participation in school sports.
headline: The claim is accurate and understates the scale. Retrieved sources confirm that 27 states have enacted statutory bans on transgender athletes in school sports, with the U.S. Supreme Court ruling 6-3 on June 30, 2026 upholding those state laws.

text: Vatican City is the smallest independent state in the world by area.
headline: This claim is accurate and directly confirmed by multiple fetched authoritative sources. Vatican City, at 0.44–0.49 km² (~49 hectares / 120 acres), is the world's smallest internationally recognized independent state by area. The second-smallest independent state, Monaco, is ~2.0 km² — roughly four times larger.

text: Church attendance in the United States has declined over the past several decades, according to Gallup polling.
headline: Confirmed accurate. Gallup's own published polling directly documents a multi-decade decline: weekly/near-weekly attendance fell from 49% (1955) to 42% (2000–2003) to 30% (2021–2023), and church membership dropped from 73% (1937) to below 50% for the first time in 2020.

text: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 outlawed discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.
headline: The claim is accurate. Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 explicitly prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin — exactly the five categories stated in the post. The Act was signed into law by President Lyndon Johnson on July 2, 1964. One important nuance: not all eleven titles of the Act cover all five categories equally. Sex was added only in Title VII (employment); other titles (e.g., Title II on public accommodations, Title VI on federal funding) address race, color, religion, and national origin but not sex. The post's five-category summary is accurate as a general characterization of the Act's best-known protections.

text: Federal data show a persistent gap in median household wealth between white and Black families in the United States.
headline: Strongly supported. The Federal Reserve's own Survey of Consumer Finances — the primary federal dataset — documents a large, persistent white-Black median wealth gap across every survey wave from 1989 through 2022. In 2022, median white family wealth was $285,000 versus $44,900 for Black families. In 2019, it was $188,200 versus $24,100. The gap has never closed in the SCF's recorded history, and in absolute dollar terms it reached its widest point in 2022.
